title: The family picture
lede: What the family owns, what it's worth, and what's owed on it, so Nicholas can build one true net worth number. Rough numbers and ranges are fine, in any order, over as many sittings as you like. If a number needs a document you don't have handy, write "need records" or "ask Dad" and move on. Never type an account number, password, or Social Security number here: say "in person" and tell him. Each part sends itself to Nicholas a few seconds after you stop typing and keeps a copy on your phone.

sections.title: 1. Properties
sections.lead: For each one: who owns it, what it's worth, what's owed. Rough numbers are fine. Never type account numbers, tell Nicholas in person.

qs.t: The warehouse (Fairhaven)
rows: Who owns it on paper (a trust, a company, a person)?
Mortgage: which bank, what's owed today, and the monthly payment
What do you think it would sell for today?
Does the business pay rent for it? To whom, and how much a year?

qs.t: The two lots next to the warehouse
rows: Who owns them on paper?
Anything owed on them?
What would they sell for today?

qs.t: The Westport Point units (ours: 2, 4, 6)
rows: Who owns our units on paper?
Mortgage: bank, balance owed today, monthly payment
What would our units sell for today?
Rent they earn per year

qs.t: Your home
rows: Mortgage: bank, balance owed today, monthly payment
Any second mortgage or home-equity line: balance owed
What would it sell for today?

qs.t: Nicholas's house
rows: First mortgage: bank, balance owed, monthly payment, whose name
Second mortgage: bank, balance owed, monthly payment, whose name

Rent it earns per year

Anything owed on it?
What would it sell for today?

qs.t: Any other property, land, or rental we haven't listed, including the house that is rented out short-term
qs.ph: A nickname is fine: who owns it, what's owed, what it would sell for, what it earns a year

sections.title: 3. Trusts and companies
sections.lead: So each asset lands under the right owner.

qs.t: The family realty trust: what it owns, and who the beneficiaries are
The family realty LLC: what it owns, and who the members are (percent each)
Any other trust, LLC, or company in the family, including one that is closed or being closed: name, what it holds, who owns it, and if closed, when
Where are the papers kept (deeds, trust papers, company papers), and who is the trustee?
qs.ph: A drawer, a lawyer's office, a safe; the trustee's role (Dad, you, a lawyer)

qs.t: Is there a will or an estate plan? With which lawyer?
qs.ph: Yes / no / not sure; the law office
